Why is this investor on the list?

I built Funding Radar to make that answer easier to inspect before sending a pitch.

Start with a startup's product, stage and country. TinySet researches comparable funding rounds. The workbench connects reviewed investments to named deal responsibility, scoped cheque policies and real founder contact routes.

One detail from the demo: Amperon's page carried a 2026 label, but the financing was announced in 2023. The original research stays visible, and the older round is excluded from the recent-deal evidence.

The walkthrough covers developer tools, energy software and payments infrastructure, plus a new live investigation. Sources, ranking reasons and qualifications sit beside the result. Human source review remains part of the process.

Built with TinyFish for Bounty Drop 002.

Code, saved research and the 100-second walkthrough:
https://github.com/himanshu748/funding-radar

discord:
I built Funding Radar for the Funding Radar bounty.

Describe the startup, then inspect the comparable rounds and the reasoning behind a reviewed investor shortlist. Each selected firm links to investment proof, a named responsible person, scoped cheque/stage evidence and a published founder route.

The demo covers US developer tools, UK energy software and India payments infrastructure. A separate genuine security-compliance run returned 19 companies; later source review supports 17. Its investor stays conditional because eligibility and current intake are unconfirmed.

TinySet discovers the company-round rows. Human source review checks their meaning. Original claims, corrections and any ordinary-web additions stay separate. JSON and CSV exports keep that provenance.

The local preview replays the saved evidence without a key. The attached 100-second video uses actual browser captures with captions.

Code and setup:
https://github.com/himanshu748/funding-radar
